texts.preamble: Satnam Singh vs State Of Punjab And Anr on 12 July, 2016 Author: Rameshwar Singh Malik Bench: Rameshwar Singh Malik Cwp No.10979 of 2016 1 In The High Court Of Punjab And Haryana At Chandigarh. Cwp No.10979 of 2016 Date of Decision : 12.7.2016 Satnam Singh ......Petitioner Vs. State of Punjab and another ......Respondents ... Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rameshwar Singh Malik ... Present : Mr. Vishal Sharma, Advocate for the petitioner. ... 1. To be referred to the Reporter or not ?
texts.facts: Facts of the case are hardly in dispute. Petitioner had been doing the business of selling the milk. The sample of cow milk drawn from the milk possessed by the petitioner failed. It is also a matter of record that the milk was found sub-standard. Petitioner was granted due opportunity of 1 of 6 being heard. He was found guilty of selling adulterated milk, because of which the Adjudicating Officer i.e. the competent authority, Gurdaspur vide order dated 26.9.2014 (Annexure P-2) imposed a fine of Rs.1.00 lac on the petitioner. Satnam Singh vs State Of Punjab And Anr on 12 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83876743/ 1 Feeling aggrieved against the above said impugned order, petitioner filed his appeal before the State Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, Punjab, Chandigarh, (for short `the appellate tribunal'), but the learned tribunal dismissed his appeal after having found the same without any merit. Hence this writ petition.
texts.arguments: The only argument raised by learned counsel for the petitioner is that the petitioner being the first offender, the fine imposed upon him is on higher side. He prays for setting aside the impugned order. Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner and after careful perusal of the record of the case, this court is of the considered opinion that both the authorities have recorded concurrent findings of fact and both the impugned orders are based on cogent findings, which call for no interference at the hands of this court. The operative part of the order dated 26.9.2014 passed by the prescribed authority, reads as under :- "8. Therefore, as per Section 68(4) while determining the quantum of penalty guidelines specified in Section 49 which are as under have to be considered :- 2 of 6 a. the amount of gain or unfair advantage wherever quantifiable, made as a result of the contravention. b. the amount of loss caused or likely to cause to any person as a result of the contravention. The operative part of the impugned order passed by the learned appellate tribunal, reads as under :- Satnam Singh vs State Of Punjab And Anr on 12 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83876743/ 2 " I have considered the said arguments. 15. Section 51 of the Act provides that if any person, 4 of 6 who, whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports any article of food for human consumption, which is sub-standard, shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to five lakh rupees. The view taken by this court also finds support from the judgement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in M/s Teri Oat Estates (P) Ltd. Vs. U.T., Chandigarh and Satnam Singh vs State Of Punjab And Anr on 12 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83876743/ 3 others, 2004 (2) SCC 130. Adulteration in the food items is a very serious issue, which causes numerous diseases and ultimately a poor consumer has to suffer.
